profile_name: Young’s Literal Translation — shadow variant selection review
method: YLT wording comparison plus targeted edition/apparatus review. Branch choice means alignment to the stored YLT translation, not a judgment of earliest reading or universal textual authority.
legacy_bridge_warning: Existing YLT rendering rows are generated by YLT-to-KJV alignment followed by inherited KJV-to-Greek positions; they are not independent YLT lexical evidence.
selection_policy: No KJV candidate selection is inherited as a YLT selection. Only explicitly reviewed proposals receive a proposed branch; all others remain null.

YLT “Judas also and Silas” does not uniquely decide τε versus δέ; both can be rendered with connective force. Printed editions differ (Nestle/WH/Byzantine use τε; Scrivener TR uses δέ). Retain unresolved pending source-edition identification.
YLT “and also her greatness” is compatible with the broader connective sequence; English does not isolate this particle reliably. Do not override from word matching alone.
We came; preserve the companion phrase witness combination.

YLT “not as writing to thee” does not establish a Greek participle. A γράφω is the finite first-person verb “I write” and is syntactically natural after “I beseech thee”; English gerund phrasing is not proof of B γράφων. Do not apply B.
